core_goal.definition: Exponential gains in intelligence per joule, defined as meaningful capability, insight, or task performance per unit of energy.
core_goal.current_baseline: Training a single frontier model consumes energy comparable to hundreds of households, and AI datacenters increasingly rival nations in power demand.
core_goal.target_metric: A 10-year roadmap for AI+HW co-design and co-development spanning algorithms, architectures, systems, and sustainability to achieve exponential gains in intelligence per joule.

key_characteristics: Hardware layer is foundation for AI efficiency, demanding radical innovation with memory-centric designs, 3D stacking, compute-in-memory, photonic interconnects, and heterogeneous coordination, driven by AI-enhanced electronic design automation.

AI must become hardware-aware while hardware becomes AI-adaptive, closing the innovation gap via AI-in-the-loop design automation, hardware-aware training, and self-evolving stacks that continuously optimize efficiency.

AI systems must ultimately serve human and planetary needs while remaining computationally sustainable; real-world applications demand constraints on energy, latency, robustness, interpretability, and cost, which drive new algorithmic paradigms and hardware targets.

short_term_2_5_years: Domain-specific AI accelerators with native support for quantization and sparsity enabling substantial performance-per-watt gains.
Heterogeneous compute nodes combining CPU, GPU, and NPU to map different AI pipeline components to the most suitable hardware, improving utilization and reducing system-level inefficiencies.
High-bandwidth memory (HBM) integration with wider interfaces and tighter coupling to compute to address memory bandwidth and data movement bottlenecks.
3D packaging and chiplet-based architectures enabling scalable composition of compute, memory, and accelerators with improved yield and flexibility.
Hardware-aware compilers, auto-tuners, and optimized operator libraries to close the gap between peak capability and achieved utilization.
Standardization across APIs, IRs, model formats, and kernel libraries to reduce fragmentation and ensure portability across heterogeneous AI systems.
Edge and on-device AI with small, efficient models for low-latency, privacy-preserving, energy-efficient inference at scale.
Hybrid unified memory hierarchies combining fast DRAM with slower NVRAM/flash for tiered access patterns and persistent state across CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators.
long_term_6_10_years: Compute-in-memory and analog computing colocate computation and storage, embracing approximate and robust algorithms for orders-of-magnitude efficiency gains.
Dense 3D integration and advanced packaging collapse distance between logic and memory, enabling fine-grained bandwidth-rich communication for new compute-memory dataflows.
Photonic and optoelectronic interconnects provide near distance-independent bandwidth and latency, removing electrical signaling bottlenecks for large-scale AI systems.
Photonic computing elements may enable new energy-efficient primitives for linear algebra and signal processing, expanding the hardware-accelerated operator set.
Quantum-accelerated AI via hybrid quantum–classical systems for optimization, sampling, and simulation tasks hard for classical scaling.
Photonic and optical interconnects within and between chips for orders-of-magnitude improvements in bandwidth density and energy efficiency.
Photonic accelerators and analog–optical hybrid computing for energy-efficient linear algebra and signal processing primitives in specialized AI workloads.
Broader adoption of compute-in-memory and analog computing to reduce data movement by colocating computation with storage, using algorithmic robustness to manage noise.
Dense 3D heterogeneous integration of compute, memory, and logic enabling new dataflows and higher system-level efficiency for emerging physical AI workloads.
New materials and transistor technologies beyond conventional CMOS, if manufacturable at scale, to overcome limits in power, speed, and integration density.
Ultra-scalable distributed AI systems with adaptive coherence and orchestration across cloud, edge, and device layers to support coordinated operation of intelligent agents.
